text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chairman of the main board of Bosnia's rulling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) Halid Genjac says that the tragic incident in the Croat controlled part of divided Bosnian town of Mostar in which one man was killed and 22 others were wounded was carried out on purpose on the eve of the decission on the disputed northern town of Brcko, in order to prove that Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation is impossible.

- Several vehicles with license plates of Croatia and self- designed Bosnian Croat state of Herceg-Bosna were attacked on the road north of the town of Mostar by an organised group of Mostar citizens helped by the local police, Croat member of Bosnia's collective presidency Kresimir Zubak says in a statement citing reports he received from Mostar's Croat police.

- "Killing and violence of people who are trying to visit graves of their families cannot be tolerated any more," an international mediator for Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Christian Schwarz-Schilling tells the daily.

- Moslem President of Mostar's city council Hamdija Jahic says he fears that all apartments inhabited by Moslems in two buildings at Croat controlled part of the town were emptied and majority of those people was taken in an unknown direction in the wave of evictions of Moslems.

- "Conflicts, killing and wounding of Mostar's Moslems caused by Bosnian Croats who prevented these people visiting graves are punch in the face to all those who are fighting for peace and consolation in Bosnia," German Minister of Foreign Affairs Klaus Kinkel tells the daily.

- Donors' conference for Bosnia scheduled to take place in Brusseles on mid March will be delayed for a month, daily cites its sources as saying. Reasons for delay are pending international arbiter's decision on the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko as well as problems of country's councill of ministers to set up the common curency and create the central bank.

- Mirsad Ceman, Secretary General of the rulling Bosnian Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) says that SDA would not be surprised if the Arbitration Tribunal gives a short-term special status to the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko.

- Valentin Coric, Bosnian Croat Cantonal Minister of Interior in Mostar region, says at a meeting that the attack on Moslem pilgrims in Croat controlled part of Mostar was led by the chief of Mostar Croat police Marko Radic, Coric's Moslem deputy Sefkija Dziho says.

- NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) suspends military training outside all barracks in Bosnia with exception of flying, in anticipation of the arbitration decision for the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko and invited all reservists to be stood down immediately and to return to their homes, an SFOR spokesman Tony White says.
